articles.title: Garba Season Is Back in Delhi: Where to Learn Dandiya Moves Ahead of Navratri
articles.excerpt: Studios across Delhi and the NCR have opened festival-season batches with Sharad Navratri starting October 11 — from Rs 1,500-a-month group classes to weekend crash workshops.
articles.image_caption: Dancers performing Garba with dandiya sticks during a Navratri celebration. Garba classes across Delhi are filling up as the festive season begins.
articles.nri_angle: Garba nights now draw thousands in the US, UK and Canada every October — the Delhi classes are the home-country version of a ritual the diaspora celebrates wherever it lives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRI Entrepreneur Dr Ronald Colaco Pitches 25-Year Coastal Master Plan for Karnataka
articles.excerpt: Dr Ronald Colaco's proposal to the Karnataka government envisages an expert-led task force — including NRI representatives — and a 20–25-year master plan for the Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and Uttara Kannada coast.
articles.nri_angle: An NRI entrepreneur driving a 25-year development vision for his home region — with NRI representatives proposed for the task force itself — shows diaspora capital and expertise shaping Karnataka's future.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Over 100,000 Floridians May Now Hold Canadian Citizenship Under New Law
articles.excerpt: Canada's Bill C-3 scrapped the first-generation limit on citizenship by descent, opening a path for Americans with Canadian ancestors — no test, no oath, just proof.
articles.image_caption: A Florida waterfront city with palm trees and a marina. Census estimates show roughly 59,000 Florida residents of Canadian ancestry and 99,000 of French Canadian ancestry, most of whom may now qualify for Canadian citizenship.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American families with Canadian roots may hold the same hidden second citizenship, offering a passport that now outranks the US one and a concrete Plan B in an uncertain immigration climate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Gastroenterologist Dr. Mukul Arya to Receive Global Healthcare Leadership Award
articles.excerpt: The White Plains Hospital director will accept the inaugural Global Healthcare Leader of the Year honor at Worldwide Community First Responder's 15th anniversary gala in Nyack on September 19.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Mukul Arya, a board-certified gastroenterologist and Director of Advanced Gastroenterology at White Plains Hospital. He will receive the inaugural Global Healthcare Leader of the Year Award at Worldwide Community First Responder’s 15th anniversary gala in Nyack on September 19.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American physician and AAPI chapter founder receives a major healthcare leadership honor in the New York medical community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Couple Gives $4 Million to University of Houston Engineering College
articles.excerpt: Manmohan Singh Kalsi and Marie-Luise Schubert Kalsi's gift to UH's Cullen College of Engineering funds professorships, fellowships and a seminar series, marking one of the largest donations to the mechanical engineering department in recent years.
articles.image_caption: The Ezekiel W. Cullen Building at the University of Houston. Manmohan Singh Kalsi and Marie-Luise Schubert Kalsi have committed $4 million to the university’s Cullen College of Engineering.
articles.nri_angle: The gift reflects a classic Houston Indian-American trajectory — graduate study at UH, decades building a company, and endowing the institution that provided the foothold — and expands fellowships and professorships feeding the city's energy and aerospace industries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: G R Balasubramaniam: Left School at 13, Built a Rs 1,000 Crore Dairy Empire
articles.excerpt: From Rs 3,000 in savings and door-to-door butter deliveries in Bengaluru to GRB Dairy Foods' Rs 1,084 crore in annual revenue — the five-decade rise of G R Balasubramaniam.
articles.image_caption: G R Balasubramaniam, founder of GRB Dairy Foods. He left school at 13 and built the company into a Rs 1,000 crore business selling ghee, sweets and snacks in more than 40 countries.
articles.nri_angle: GRB Dairy Foods exports ghee, sweets and spices to 40+ countries including Singapore, Australia and the UAE, where diaspora shoppers are core customers; the founder's journey is a case study for diaspora entrepreneurs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From US Software Job to Rs 36 Lakh Moringa Farm in Maharashtra
articles.excerpt: Sagar Khare walked away from a high-paying American tech job, returned to his village in Solapur, and built a profitable organic moringa business on five acres.
articles.image_caption: Drumstick pods on a moringa tree. Software engineer Sagar Khare grows organic moringa on five acres in Solapur, Maharashtra, earning about Rs 36 lakh a year.
articles.nri_angle: A reverse-migration story: an NRI software engineer leaves the US corporate track for organic farming in Maharashtra, offering a template for diaspora professionals considering a return.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chinmaya Mission's 75th Anniversary: How Atlanta's Diaspora Chanted the Gita Together
articles.excerpt: More than 2,000 devotees gathered in Suwanee, Georgia, for an evening of mass Gita chanting, music and dance as part of the movement's year-long 75th anniversary commemoration.
articles.image_caption: A copy of the Bhagavad Gita. More than 2,000 devotees chanted Chapter 15 of the Gita at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav in Suwanee, Georgia.
articles.nri_angle: Atlanta's Chinmaya community, 25 years strong with 1,000+ children in weekly classes, anchored the Mission's 75th anniversary celebrations in the US Southeast.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Envoy Sergio Gor: India Relationship Stronger Than Five Years Ago
articles.excerpt: In an interview with India Today, US Ambassador Sergio Gor argues the strategic partnership has deepened across trade, defence and technology — and says the interim trade deal is effectively done.
articles.image_caption: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor. The envoy told India Today that the US-India relationship is 'stronger than it was five years ago,' pointing to deeper cooperation on trade, defence and technology.
articles.nri_angle: Gor's reassurance that the H-1B review is a broad overhaul rather than India-targeted speaks directly to the hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals on US work visas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At 4, Treesha Thosar Breaks Kamal Haasan's Record as Youngest National Award Winner
articles.excerpt: Treesha Vivek Thosar received the Best Child Artist honour at the 71st National Film Awards for her role as Chimi in the Marathi film Naal 2, surpassing a record Kamal Haasan had held since 1960.
articles.image_caption: President Droupadi Murmu presents the National Film Award to four-year-old Treesha Thosar at the ceremony, with a portrait of the young winner alongside. Treesha broke Kamal Haasan's record to become the youngest National Award winner.

sources.label: Times of India — Meet Treesha Thosar
Mint — Youngest National Film Award winner
Bollywood Hungama — Kamal Haasan congratulates Treesha Thosar

articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, a four-year-old Marathi actor setting a national record is a point of cultural pride and a way for diaspora families to celebrate Indian cinema's young talent with their own children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Finland Courts Indian Students With Work Rights, Family Visas and Affordable Tuition
articles.excerpt: As the US, UK, Canada and Australia tighten student rules, Finland is pitching Indian students a steadier deal: 30 hours of weekly work during study, a two-year post-study job search, and family residence permits. Here is what the numbers actually say.
articles.image_caption: The University of Helsinki. Finland is courting Indian students with work rights, family visas, and affordable tuition.
articles.nri_angle: Indian families get a rare combination — generous student work rights, a two-year post-study job search, and family residence permits — but must weigh tuition costs against a proposed 2027 family-reunification waiting period.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Virat Kohli Meets Maharashtra Deputy CM Eknath Shinde in London
articles.excerpt: The goodwill meeting during Shinde's UK visit covered sports, infrastructure, and state welfare schemes; the Deputy CM felicitated Kohli with a shawl and bouquet.
articles.image_caption: Virat Kohli. The India star met Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde during his visit to London.
articles.nri_angle: Kohli, who lives in London, and Shinde's diaspora-facing announcements underscore the UK Indian community's role as a bridge between Indian politics and its global audience.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bengaluru Techie's Website Reunites Nepal Flood Victims' Families With Data
articles.excerpt: ReuniteIndia.com consolidates scattered official records into a single searchable database of people missing in the Nepal floods, with QR-coded live case pages.
articles.image_caption: Flood-hit areas in Nepal. A Bengaluru techie's website has been reuniting families separated by the flooding.
articles.nri_angle: Many of the missing are Telangana-origin NRIs and Kailash pilgrims, making a single verified English-language database vital for diaspora families searching from abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stalker Kills Sacramento Woman Despite Restraining Order; Mother Blames System
articles.excerpt: Shalini Thakur, 38, was shot outside a Panera Bread in Sacramento after months of alleged stalking by 22-year-old Rohit Rohit, who later died by suicide in a police standoff.
articles.image_caption: Downtown Sacramento. A woman was killed by a stalker despite a restraining order, prompting questions about enforcement gaps.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin woman working a service job in California was killed by her alleged stalker despite a restraining order, raising urgent safety questions for immigrant workers in the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala Crash Kills NRI Family of Three; 36-Hour Arrest Delay Raises Questions
articles.excerpt: The deaths of Gulf returnee Muneer, his wife and their 3-year-old son have revived questions about delayed alcohol evidence — echoing the 2019 Venkitaraman case.
articles.image_caption: A national highway in Kerala. Gulf returnee Muneer, 35, his wife Shafna, 25, and their 3-year-old son died on the Kunnamkulam–Guruvayur road when a car rammed their motorcycle late on September 5.
articles.nri_angle: Muneer was a Gulf returnee — his death resonates across Kerala's diaspora, where nearly every family has someone working abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eiffel Tower Gender Row Over BAPS Visit Unites French Politicians, Splits Diaspora
articles.excerpt: A private BAPS visit to the Eiffel Tower that sidelined female staff united French politicians across the spectrum — while splitting the Indian diaspora over accountability and backlash.
articles.image_caption: The Eiffel Tower in Paris. A row over a BAPS visit to the monument has united French politicians while splitting opinion in the diaspora.
articles.nri_angle: The row has split Indians in France between those warning against anti-Hindu backlash and those insisting BAPS must be held accountable without conflating it with Hinduism.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bank of America Pilots Zelle-UPI Bridge to Speed NRI Remittances to India
articles.excerpt: Bank of America and Early Warning Services are piloting a link between the US instant-payment network Zelle and India's UPI, promising faster, cheaper remittances for NRIs — though the service is not yet publicly available.
articles.image_caption: Bank of America signage on a glass office building. The bank is working with Zelle network operator Early Warning Services on a pilot that would connect the US instant-payment system with India's UPI network for NRI remittances.
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indian professionals in the US remit money home monthly; a native Zelle-to-UPI channel would let them do it inside their banking app with faster settlement and lower cost.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pooja Sethi Wins Primary, One Step from Historic Texas House Seat
articles.excerpt: The Indian American immigration attorney defeated a 20-year Army veteran for the Democratic nomination in Texas House District 47 and would be the first Indian American to serve in the Texas Legislature if she wins in November.
articles.image_caption: A "Pooja Sethi for Texas" campaign sign beside a portrait of Sethi. Sethi won the primary and is one step away from a historic Texas House seat.
articles.nri_angle: Sethi's run marks a milestone for Indian American political representation in Texas and shows how diaspora professionals are converting organizing and legislative staff work into electoral power.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Started at 12, Now 300,000 Strong: India's Children-Led Digital Art Museum
articles.excerpt: The Children's Art Museum of India, launched by two teenagers in 2022, has grown into a 300,000-member community of young artists — and it has never raised a rupee of investor funding.
articles.image_caption: A portrait of Krish Nawal, co-founder of the Children's Art Museum of India, set against a wall of framed children's paintings. CAMI has grown from a project started by two teenagers into a digital community of more than 300,000 members.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families can use CAMI as a bridge for their children to create art, take part in challenges, and learn about traditional Indian art forms from anywhere in the world.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Truck Driver Charged in Ohio Crash That Killed Woman, 50
articles.excerpt: Manjit Singh, 39, of Fresno, California, faces an aggravated vehicular homicide charge after a September 2 head-on collision on US 68; ICE has lodged a detainer as DHS ties the case to federal immigration policy.
articles.nri_angle: A fatal Ohio crash involving an Indian-origin truck driver has become the latest flashpoint in the national debate over immigration enforcement and commercial driver's license rules.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Couple's $20 Million Gift Creates AI College at Texas University
articles.excerpt: Anuradha and Vikas Sinha's donation to the University of North Texas will establish a new College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics backed by six permanent endowments.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American couple's $20 million gift to the University of North Texas shows how immigrant success stories are increasingly shaping American higher education philanthropy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gujarat-Origin New York Man Pleads Guilty in $9.36M Missouri Gambling Racket
articles.excerpt: Sunilkumar N Patel, 53, admitted running six Missouri arcades as a front for illegal gambling that generated $9.36 million, and now faces up to 20 years in federal prison.
articles.image_caption: A gavel rests on a sound block in a courtroom. Gujarat-origin New York resident Sunilkumar N. Patel pleaded guilty in federal court in Missouri to charges in a $9.36 million illegal gambling ring.
articles.nri_angle: Another high-profile federal fraud case involving an Indian-origin defendant in the US — a pattern that shapes perceptions of the diaspora and draws community attention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Funds Its Startups Lavishly. So Why Won't It Buy From Them?
articles.excerpt: Startups won under 4% of Rs 5.03 lakh crore in government marketplace purchases last year despite a decade of funding schemes. The problem, a new analysis argues, isn't capital — it's that no one has to buy.
articles.image_caption: An illustration shows a startup founder facing a 'Government Procurement' gate marked with tender and compliance hurdles. The article argues India funds its startups lavishly but rarely buys from them.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora founders and Indian-origin deep-tech investors eyeing India as a first customer face exactly this friction: the state funds but won't buy — access to customers, not capital, is the binding constraint.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Who Says There's No Theft in US?': Indian Family's Car Found Without Wheels
articles.excerpt: The woman woke to find the family's parked car resting on supports with all four wheels gone — and a note left behind warning of a string of thefts at the parking lot.
articles.nri_angle: Many Indian families live in US apartment complexes with shared parking lots, and the incident has resonated widely with the diaspora — a familiar reminder that crime is a fact of life everywhere, not just back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India-Canada Trade Deal by End of 2026 Is 'Very Realistic,' Envoy Says
articles.excerpt: High Commissioner Chris Cooter says the political push from Prime Ministers Modi and Carney, plus strong business interest, makes the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement timeline achievable.
articles.nri_angle: A completed CEPA would directly benefit the Indo-Canadian business community through easier movement of goods, services, and professionals between the two countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chidambaram Questions India's BRICS Gains; BJP Calls It 'Disgruntled Uncle' Attitude
articles.excerpt: P. Chidambaram said the last two or three BRICS summits delivered no tangible benefits for India. BJP leader Ram Madhav fired back with a "naraz phupha" jibe as the 2026 New Delhi summit approaches.
articles.image_caption: YouTube / CNN-News18
articles.nri_angle: BRICS debates shape trade, energy and investment conditions that directly affect NRI households, and India's 2026 chairmanship puts New Delhi's agenda-setting in the spotlight for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala NRI Panel Warns Job Seekers as Visa Scams Top Complaint List
articles.excerpt: Over 30% of the 268 complaints received this year involve financial fraud built on fake work-visa promises, chairperson Sophy Thomas said.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of a smartphone with a prohibition symbol over a job listing. Kerala’s NRI Commission says visa and job-recruitment fraud accounts for over 30% of the complaints it received this year.
articles.nri_angle: Kerala's vast Gulf diaspora is the prime target of these rackets; the commission's data shows visa fraud is now the single largest complaint category.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Couple Gives $20 Million to Create AI College at UNT
articles.excerpt: Anuradha and Vikas Sinha's gift to the University of North Texas will establish the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics — the couple's third major investment in the university that educated them.
articles.image_caption: Anuradha Sinha and Dr. Vikas Sinha pose for a photograph. The Indian-origin couple donated $20 million to the University of North Texas to establish the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-immigrant couple who came to the U.S. as students are now endowing a named AI college — a landmark example of diaspora philanthropy paying forward the opportunities international education gave them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Author Neal Bakshi Says He Was Detained at US Border After Greenland Holiday
articles.excerpt: The entrepreneur and US citizen, who holds Global Entry clearance, described being pulled into a windowless room with other people of colour and questioned about his affiliations.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American citizen's border detention despite Global Entry clearance has heightened fears of racial profiling among Indian diaspora travellers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shots Fired at Ammy Virk's Convoy After Canada Concert, Singer Escapes Unhurt
articles.excerpt: Abbotsford police are investigating after multiple rounds were fired at a vehicle in the Punjabi singer-actor's convoy following his concert in British Columbia on September 5.
articles.image_caption: Punjabi singer and actor Ammy Virk. Shots were fired at his convoy after a concert in Canada, though the singer was unharmed.
articles.nri_angle: The incident raises safety concerns for Indian performers touring abroad, particularly in Canada where the Punjabi diaspora forms a major concert audience.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Envoy Meets Bangladesh President as Teesta Water Diplomacy Takes Centre Stage
articles.excerpt: High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi's first meeting with President Alamgir focused on fair sharing of common river waters ahead of the Ganga Water Treaty renewal.
articles.image_caption: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi meets Bangladesh President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir at Bangabhaban on September 8, 2026. The meeting focused on bilateral ties and fair sharing of common river waters.
articles.nri_angle: The India-Bangladesh diplomatic reset has direct implications for the large Bangladeshi diaspora and for Indians with business, family and cultural ties across the border.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How NRI Pensioners Can Submit Life Certificates Without Traveling to India
articles.excerpt: The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare provides four alternative routes for pensioners living abroad to keep their Employees' Pension Scheme payments active.
articles.image_caption: India's Employees' Provident Fund Organisation manages the EPS-95 pension scheme. NRI pensioners must submit an annual life certificate to continue receiving payments.
articles.nri_angle: Directly affects NRI retirees who depend on Indian pension payments but cannot travel to India annually for mandatory life certificate submission.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NPS for NRIs: What Happens to Your Retirement Account When You Move Abroad
articles.excerpt: PFRDA allows NRIs to continue their NPS Tier I accounts through NRE or NRO bank accounts, but Tier II is off-limits — and renouncing citizenship triggers separate closure rules.
articles.image_caption: India's National Pension System. NRIs who return to India or move abroad face specific rules around their NPS accounts, withdrawals and tax treatment.
articles.nri_angle: Directly answers a common question for Indians moving abroad: whether their NPS savings are accessible and what restrictions apply.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hera CEO Jenny Lee's Jaipur Wedding to Indian-Origin Entrepreneur Goes Viral
articles.excerpt: Jenny Lee of healthcare startup Hera and Sagar Jajoo of Silna Health married in a multi-day Jaipur celebration blending Western and Hindu traditions, with her sangeet dance drawing over 700,000 Instagram views.
articles.image_caption: Image: @ndtv via X
articles.nri_angle: Two UC Berkeley graduates — one American, one Indian-origin — both building healthcare startups in New York, chose Jaipur for a cross-cultural wedding that blended Christian and Hindu traditions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Madras Opens 17 Online Courses to Class 9 Students for First Time
articles.excerpt: The October 2026 cohort of IIT Madras's School Connect programme extends eligibility to Class 9, offering eight-week courses across 17 disciplines from Data Science to Aerospace.
articles.image_caption: YouTube / IIT Madras BS Insider
articles.nri_angle: Online format makes IIT Madras's School Connect accessible to diaspora families exploring Indian academic pathways for their children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gujarat-Born Scientist Karim Maredia Wins Borlaug CAST Communication Award
articles.excerpt: The Michigan State University professor and dairy farmer's son from rural Gujarat has spent 35 years bridging agricultural science with communities across 60 countries.
articles.image_caption: Michigan State University, where Gujarat-born scientist Karim Maredia is a professor of entomology. He has won the Borlaug CAST Communication Award for his work in integrated pest management.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American scientist who grew up as a dairy farmer's son in Gujarat is recognised for three decades of making agricultural research accessible to farmers worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Banker Rishi Madlani Enters Race for Keir Starmer's London Seat
articles.excerpt: The sustainable finance executive and former Camden councillor is among several candidates vying for Labour's nomination in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election.
articles.image_caption: Rishi Madlani, an Indian-origin banker who has entered the race to succeed former PM Keir Starmer as Labour MP for Holborn and St Pancras.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin British banker with roots in Uganda's expelled Asian community seeks to succeed a former PM in a high-profile London parliamentary seat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nearly 90 US Politicians Pledge to Reject RSS-Linked Donations After Bhagwat's Madison Square Garden Rally
articles.excerpt: The bipartisan pledge, led by Hindus for Human Rights Action and SACRED Acts, has sparked backlash from Hindu American groups who call it discriminatory profiling.
articles.image_caption: Demonstrators protest outside Madison Square Garden during RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's rally on August 29, 2026 in New York City. Nearly 90 U.S. politicians have since pledged to reject RSS-linked campaign donations.
articles.nri_angle: About 90 US politicians pledged to reject RSS-linked campaign donations, sparking a fierce debate among Indian Americans over religious profiling and political participation ahead of the 2026 midterms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Who Is Anil Chakravarthy? The Bengaluru Boy Who Became a Chancellor's Gold Medalist, an MIT PhD, a Silicon Valley CEO — and Now Adobe's Next Leader
articles.excerpt: Adobe's board has named Anil Chakravarthy as its next president and CEO, making him the second consecutive Indian-origin leader at the helm of the creative software giant. His journey from Basavanagudi to the C-suite is a story of quiet, methodical ambition.
articles.image_caption: Anil Chakravarthy, who has been named Adobe's next CEO effective December 1, 2026, succeeding Shantanu Narayen.
articles.nri_angle: Adobe's CEO succession from one Indian-origin leader to another underscores the growing dominance of Indian-educated executives in global tech leadership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: London Court Clears Extradition of Indian-Origin Pharmacist Accused of Arsenic Murder in Hyderabad
articles.excerpt: Ajith Kumar Mupparapu, 46, faces charges of killing his ex-mother-in-law with poisoned spices and plotting to assassinate her father through contract killers and staged accidents.
articles.image_caption: A UK court building in London. A Westminster magistrate has cleared the extradition of an Indian-origin pharmacist accused of poisoning her mother-in-law with arsenic in Hyderabad.
articles.nri_angle: The case highlights the cross-border legal exposure faced by members of the Indian diaspora in the UK and the effectiveness of extradition treaties between India and Britain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York's Erasing Borders Dance Festival Returns for 18th Year With Seven Classical Indian Forms
articles.excerpt: The Indo-American Arts Council's flagship event brings Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Mohiniyattam, and more to Hunter College on September 19–20.
articles.image_caption: Dancers perform at the Indo-American Arts Council's Erasing Borders Dance Festival in New York. The 18th edition features seven classical and contemporary Indian dance forms on September 19-20, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The festival is one of the most accessible showcases for Indian classical dance in North America, giving diaspora audiences a direct connection to seven traditional art forms in a single weekend.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
